statement.p: A line is parallel to the line passing through {\left(-3,3\right)} and {\left(5,1\right)}\text{,} and passes through {\left(-8,-4\right)}\text{.}

solution.p: Based on the points {\left(-3,3\right)} and {\left(5,1\right)}\text{,} the first line has slope {-{\frac{1}{4}}}\text{.} But the lines are parallel, so the second line also has slope {-{\frac{1}{4}}}\text{.} The second line passes through {\left(-8,-4\right)}\text{,} so we can use point-slope form to write an equation for it: y={-\left(0.25\mathopen{}\left(x+8\right)+4\right)}\text{.} To plot this, we can start at {\left(-8,-4\right)} and use slope triangles.
